evidence.claim: Ethiopian authorities revoked Tom Gardner's press accreditation on May 13 and forced him to leave the country.
evidence.title: Ethiopia expels Economist correspondent Tom Gardner
evidence.excerpt: Ethiopian authorities revoked Tom Gardner's press accreditation on May 13 and forced him to leave the country.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist press-freedom monitor; the event is dated, specific, and corroborated by the outlet and regulator.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about press access under the Abiy government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The action was taken by the Ethiopian Media Authority, a statutory regulator operating under the state; attribution to Abiy is strongest as a government-pattern action, not a personally documented order.
contrary_evidence: The authority said Gardner had failed professional standards and was willing to license another correspondent.
The government could frame the move as a regulatory, not political, decision.

evidence.claim: As of November 4, 2022, authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years.
evidence.title: Two years of internet shutdowns: people in Tigray, Ethiopia, deserve better
evidence.excerpt: As of November 4, 2022, authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Leading shutdown monitor with a precise, time-stamped, region-specific claim.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within target-year 2022 and describing an ongoing restriction that remained in force during most of the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The shutdown is attributed to Ethiopian authorities; the evidence does not identify Abiy personally ordering it, but it is a federal policy choice within his government's authority.
contrary_evidence: Government officials have cited war-time disinformation and security concerns as justification for the blackout.
The article notes peace talks and calls for restoring access, so the network closure was contested.

evidence.claim: The national dialogue excluded key rebel groups, and opposition figures accused the government of trying to orchestrate the process and control who participated.
evidence.title: Ethiopia launches a national dialogue, but divisions run deep
evidence.excerpt: The national dialogue excluded key rebel groups, and opposition figures accused the government of trying to orchestrate the process and control who participated.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Field reporting with named interlocutors, concrete dates, and direct quotations from critics and the commission.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 with retrospective context from late 2021 on commission formation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The article attributes the process to Abiy's government and his public push for the dialogue, but also records that the commission claimed independence; attribution is mixed and not equivalent to a proven personal directive.
contrary_evidence: The commission and government argued the dialogue was inclusive and open to peaceful participants.
The report also notes some observers saw the process as potentially useful if managed properly.

evidence.claim: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration.
evidence.title: National Dialogue Commission, Civil Society Organizations Council Ink Partnership Agreement
evidence.excerpt: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official contemporaneous report on a formal government-supported institutional step; credible for the existence of the agreement, less so for its effectiveness.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about political-process institutions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects a state-backed institutional initiative under Abiy's government; it is strong for formal commitment, weaker for proving independent operation or actual openness.
contrary_evidence: The agreement does not show that the dialogue was truly independent or inclusive in practice.
Earlier and later reporting still described exclusion and control concerns.

evidence.claim: The PMO said the South Africa peace agreement would move Ethiopia forward on the reform path and reaffirmed commitment to peace and implementation.
evidence.title: Expression of Gratitude on the Conclusion of Peace Talks
evidence.publisher: FDRE Office of the Prime Minister
evidence.excerpt: The PMO said the South Africa peace agreement would move Ethiopia forward on the reform path and reaffirmed commitment to peace and implementation.
evidence.source_locator: Press Releases page, Dec. 1, 2022 item, lines 35-38
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement by the PM office, strong for the fact of the commitment but self-serving on sincerity.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period 2022; issued immediately after the peace talks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Abiy office statement; shows his public commitment, but not independent proof of personal candor.
contrary_evidence: Subsequent reporting still questioned full implementation and included continuing distrust around the ceasefire process.

evidence.claim: Abiy told parliament he would implement the ceasefire honestly and said the truce was needed so peace would be sustainable.
evidence.title: Ethiopia's Abiy vows 'honest' implementation of Tigray truce
evidence.excerpt: Abiy told parliament he would implement the ceasefire honestly and said the truce was needed so peace would be sustainable.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on Abiy's own parliamentary remarks, with precise date and direct quotation context.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period 2022, after the November ceasefire agreement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler statement; supports public commitment and correction, but sincerity remains inferred.
contrary_evidence: Other 2022 reporting described incomplete implementation and continued skepticism about the government's peace process.

evidence.claim: Abiy said the government created a national committee to coordinate an anti-corruption campaign, investigate officials and bribe givers/takers, and bring culprits before court.
evidence.title: Gov't Establishes National Committee To Coordinate Anti-Corruption Campaign
evidence.excerpt: Abiy said the government created a national committee to coordinate an anti-corruption campaign, investigate officials and bribe givers/takers, and bring culprits before court.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statement with specific anti-corruption actions, but it remains self-reported and not an independent audit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct statement of his anti-corruption posture; proves initiative, not effectiveness or personal non-corruption.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House and other monitors still described weak transparency and corruption problems in the same period.

evidence.claim: Ahmed Shide had served as Ethiopia's finance minister since 2018 and previously held several finance and transport posts; the profile also lists economics and development credentials.
evidence.title: Ahmed Shide
evidence.excerpt: Ahmed Shide had served as Ethiopia's finance minister since 2018 and previously held several finance and transport posts; the profile also lists economics and development credentials.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Institutional biography with specific role history and qualifications; strong on competence, weak on ruler motive.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the 2022 cabinet and its continuity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports the inference that Abiy retained a long-serving technocratic minister, but it does not rule out cronyism elsewhere.
contrary_evidence: One technocratic appointment does not establish a generally merit-based or integrity-preserving cabinet.

No public 2022 compliance trail for asset disclosure, conflicts of interest, or procurement/audit findings tied to Abiy.
